newsitem.title: GABON: Gabon legislative election on December 1.
newsitem.headline: Gabon legislative election on December 1.

text.p: Gabon will hold a much-delayed general election on December 1, officials at the Central African oil-producing nation's electoral commission said on Friday.
The election, originally planned for Sunday, had been put back because of lack of adequate preparations, they added.

The government of President Omar Bongo and his opposition rivals struck a peace deal in Paris in 1994 to put behind them political violence that marred the start of the democratic experiment in the nation of 1.2 million people.

Municipal elections took place on October 20 but the election commission scrapped results for the capital Libreville, where polling was chaotic. A rerun there and in Fougamou, where a fight prevented voting, takes place on November 24.
Bongo's Gabonese Democratic Party and the opposition Woodcutters' Party won most seats elsewhere.

The Paris accords, approved in 1995 by referendum, were designed to increase transparency in the election process. Parliament's mandate ran out in May. A second round of the legislative poll is planned for December 15.
Bongo became president in 1968 on the death of Gabon's independence president, Leon Mba, and set up a one-party state.
He began moves towards a multi-party system in 1990 after a rash or strikes and demonstrations by students and workers.
He won a five-year term in a disputed 1993 poll which triggered opposition protests. Five people died in the unrest.

Further clashes followed in 1994, in part to back demands for pay rises after the devaluation that year of the CFA franc used in much of French-speaking Africa. The official death toll was nine, the opposition put the toll at 38.
